title: Python Numerical Data Types
description: Test your knowledge on Python numerical data types: int, float, and complex numbers.

questions.question: What is the data type of the value 42 in Python?
questions.explanation: In Python, 42 is an integer (int) because it has no decimal point.

questions.question: Which of the following creates a complex number in Python?
questions.explanation: The complex() function can be used to create a complex number in Python.

questions.question: What will be the output of: type(3.0)?
questions.explanation: 3.0 contains a decimal point, so it is a float.

questions.question: Which code correctly checks if a number is a float?
questions.explanation: Both isinstance(x, float) and type(x) == float can be used.

questions.question: In Python, what does 2 + 3j represent?
questions.explanation: The j suffix indicates the imaginary part, so this is a complex number.

questions.question: What will be the output of: isinstance(5, int)?
questions.explanation: 5 is an integer, so isinstance(5, int) returns True.

questions.question: Which statement correctly converts 5.7 into an integer?
questions.explanation: The int() function converts a float to an integer by truncating the decimal part.

questions.question: What is the output of: (3+4j).real?
questions.explanation: .real returns the real part of a complex number, which is 3.0.

questions.question: Which function is used to find the absolute value of a number in Python?
questions.explanation: abs() is the built-in Python function to find the absolute value.

questions.question: What is the output of: type(3+0j)?
questions.explanation: Even though the imaginary part is 0, 3+0j is still a complex number.
